Agent Skills

## You've been using skills all day {.center}

When you asked Posit Assistant for help today, it loaded `.agents/skills/help/SKILL.md`.

::: fragment
A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file: a description of when to use it, plus instructions for how to do the job.
:::

::: notes
Open `.agents/skills/help/SKILL.md` live and scroll through it. Attendees have been on the receiving end of this skill all morning.

The same format works across agents: Posit Assistant, Claude Code, and many others follow the Agent Skills spec.

Skills are plain markdown, checked into your project — no packaging, no build step.
:::

## Anatomy of a skill

```
skills/
└── renewal-letters/
    ├── SKILL.md      # Required: metadata + instructions
    ├── scripts/      # Optional: executable code
    ├── references/   # Optional: documentation
    └── assets/       # Optional: templates, data files
```

## SKILL.md

````markdown
---
name: renewal-letters
description: Draft a renewal letter for a lapsed Last Blockbuster member.
---

# Renewal letters

Offer Basic members a free-rental code.
Offer Family members a family-night bundle.
Offer Founders members a commemorative card.
````

::: footer
[Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification){preview-link=true}
:::

::: notes
Two required frontmatter fields:

- `name`: lowercase, hyphens, max 64 characters, must match the folder name.
- `description`: max 1024 characters, and it must say what the skill does AND when to use it.

The description is the only thing the agent sees at startup, so it decides whether your skill ever gets used.

The body is free markdown: steps, rules, gotchas, a template.
:::

## Progressive disclosure {.center}

::: incremental
1. **Discovery** — the agent loads only each skill's `name` and `description` (~100 tokens each)

1. **Activation** — when a task matches, the agent reads the full `SKILL.md`

1. **Execution** — instructions run; extra files load only when the skill asks for them
:::

::: notes
This is why skills scale: you can keep 100 skills on hand for the cost of their descriptions.

The full instructions load only when a task calls for them.

Same idea you'll implement by hand in the exercise: the system prompt lists the skill, a tool loads the body.

## Why not just use the system prompt?

::: incremental
* The system prompt is **always** in context — every token, every request

* Skills load **on demand** — only when a task matches

* So skills let you give an agent deep expertise without paying for it up front
:::

::: notes
You wrote a system prompt for the Blockbuster agent. That works for one small set of rules.

Now imagine 50 jobs: renewal letters, store opening procedures, staff notes, rental policies, and social media voice.

Stuffed into the system prompt, they crowd out the conversation and cost tokens on every request.

As skills, they cost about 100 tokens each until the moment one is needed.
:::

## Writing a skill that works

::: incremental
* **Add what the agent lacks; omit what it knows** — no "write clear descriptions"

* **Description says what and when** — it's the trigger

* **Concrete beats generic** — a template, a rule, a gotcha

* **Keep it short** — under 500 lines; push detail to `references/`
:::

::: footer
[Best practices for skill creators](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices){preview-link=true}
:::

::: notes
The test for every line: would the agent get this wrong without it?

If the agent already writes clean markdown, don't tell it to write clean markdown.

Give a default, not a menu: one way to do it, with an escape hatch.

Gotchas are the highest-value content: the environment-specific facts that defy reasonable assumptions.
:::

## The scene: win-back letters {.center}

Your win-back work paid off and found three Founders members we really want to keep.
Your job is to write those letters.

| Member | Tier | Last rented |
|:----------|:-------|:------------------|
| Elaine Wu | Founders | The Princess Bride |
| Theo Bennett | Founders | The Matrix |
| Marisol Vega | Founders | The Goonies |

::: notes
This is the ground truth for the exercise: the win-back list from the last round narrowed to three members, and all three are Founders tier — the ones we most want to keep — so each letter should offer the commemorative card, not a free-rental code or family bundle.

A good letter also greets the member by name, references their last rented title, invites them back, and never mentions overdue fees or unlisted discounts. Letters land in `letters/drafts/`, named like `elaine-wu.md`.

You don't need to read the skill or the CSVs in detail to judge the agent: right three people, right perk, warm voice, no fee talk, three files.

If your agent drafts for a Basic member like Malik Johnson, or invents a tier fact, you'll now spot it immediately.
:::

# Your Turn `21_skills-1` {.slide-your-turn}

1. Your Blockbuster agent gets a skill: `renewal-letters` holds the letter-writing instructions.

1. List the skill in the system prompt, and give the agent a tool to read it.

1. Draft letters for the top three lapsed members. Watch the agent read the skill **before** it starts drafting — and check them against the scene we just saw.

{{< countdown 5:00 left=0 bottom="-2em" >}}

::: notes
The read_skill tool is like the read_file tool, pointed at the skills folder.

The system prompt listing is the manual version of what real harnesses generate automatically at startup.

The trace should show read_skill firing when the agent starts the letter task.
:::

## Discussion: Did your agent...? {.center}

::: incremental
* Read the skill **before** it drafted a single letter?

* Pick the right top three members from `lapsed.csv`?

* Invent tier facts — a Founders perk for someone who isn't one?

* Mention overdue fees, even though the skill forbids it?

* Leave the data files untouched?
:::

::: notes
Stress-test evidence, five runs: the mechanism you built works — `read_skill` fired first in every single run, before any drafting.

But the agent picked the wrong "top three" in one of five runs, drafting for Malik Johnson instead of Elaine Wu — reading the file isn't the same as reading it carefully.

That same run compounded the error: it called a Basic-tier member "one of our Founders members" and gave him a commemorative card. Wrong pick, wrong perk.

Another run wrote "late fees we won't dwell on" in a letter — a direct brush with the skill's no-fees rule.

The good news: in all five runs the data files were left untouched, tool calls were clean, and four of five letter sets were correct.

Close on the failure modes: skills load reliably, but grounding — who are the top three, what tier are they — still depends on the agent checking its sources.
:::

# Your Turn `22_skills-2` {.slide-your-turn}

1. The skill has been swapped for a **first draft** with common problems.

1. Use the diagnostic questions to fix `SKILL.md`, then re-run the letter task.

1. Compare: same agent, same tools, different skill, different letters and token spend.

{{< countdown 5:00 left=0 bottom="-2em" >}}

::: notes
The planted problems: the description is background about the manager's notes, while the actual trigger sits in the body. The body also repeats policies, generic advice, and conflicting process instructions.

Four questions lead attendees from the misplaced trigger to the repeated facts and conflicting process. They move and delete text; they do not need to invent new instructions.

The good skill says when to draft a renewal letter and keeps only the voice, letter structure, tier incentives, filename rule, and promises caveat.
:::

## Skills in Posit Assistant

::: incremental
* Built-ins: `create-skill`, `r-package-development`, `quarto-authoring`, ...

* Yours: `~/.posit/assistant/skills/` (all projects) or `.agents/skills/` (this project)

* Most skills also run as slash commands: `/renewal-letters`
:::

::: footer
[Skills — Posit Assistant docs](https://assistant.posit.co/docs/features/skills/){preview-link=true}
:::

::: notes
`.agents/skills/` is the portable location: any spec-following agent can read it.

The built-in create-skill skill walks you through making a new one interactively.

Skills double as commands when you want to trigger a workflow deliberately instead of hoping the model picks it.
:::

## Skills in the ecosystem

| Layer | What it carries | When it loads |
|:----------|:----------------|:--------------|
| System prompt | Core behavior | Always |
| **Skills** | Procedures, house rules, expertise | On demand |
| MCP servers | Connections to external tools | Registered per tool call |

::: notes
Rough map, from the Posit open-source AI newsletter.

AGENTS.md and the system prompt shape everything the agent does.

Skills carry the long tail of knowledge: too specific to always pay for, too valuable to leave out.

MCP servers are about tools — connections to databases, APIs, other software. Bonus material covers MCP.
:::

## Skills, recap

::: incremental
* A skill is a folder with `SKILL.md`: metadata plus instructions

* Progressive disclosure: descriptions at startup, body on demand

* Write what the agent doesn't know — and say when to use it

* Same format in Posit Assistant, Claude Code, and any spec-following agent
:::

::: notes
You built the mechanism yourself today: listing, loading, and writing skills.

:::
